title: Prime-to-ell residue-degree locus of an etale morphism is constructible
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning that it admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\ell$ be a prime, and let $f:Y\to X$ be an étale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The subset
$$\operatorname{dec}_{\ell' }(f)=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ f(y)=x,\ [\kappa(y):\kappa(x)]\text{ is finite and not divisible by }\ell\}$$
[def-weil-residue-field] is ind-constructible (a union of locally closed subsets), equivalently it is open in the constructible topology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology]. No quasi-compactness or separation assumption is imposed on $Y$ or $f$.

source.place: Expose II, Proposition 2.2.2, printed p. 26: for an étale morphism over a Noetherian scheme, the prime-to-ell decomposed locus is ind-constructible.
